title: Add pcb_stackup element for fabricator stackup and material data
description: Adds a new pcb_stackup element to Circuit JSON for carrying resolved physical layer data alongside the board, allowing consumers to access material properties without needing to re-resolve templates or read side files.
body:
## Why

Downstream projects such as `0hmX/am3352-ddr-eye` keep board construction and material properties in a separate `board-construction.json` / `simulation.json`. This PR adds `pcb_stackup`, so Circuit JSON can carry the resolved physical layer data alongside the board. A follow-up in core/props will resolve a fabricator template code, such as JLCPCB `JLC04161H-3313`, and emit the full stackup. Consumers can then use those values without re-resolving the template or reading a side file.

## Schema

- Identifiers: `pcb_stackup_id`, `pcb_board_id`, optional `subcircuit_id`.
- Optional `plated_hole_copper_thickness`: the copper thickness of plated hole and via barrel walls.
- Required `layers`, ordered top to bottom, discriminated by `layer_type`:
  - `soldermask`: `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`
  - `copper`: `layer` (`top`, `inner1`, …, `bottom`), `thickness`, `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m`, `rms_surface_roughness`
  - `dielectric`: `dielectric_type` (`core` | `prepreg`), `material_name`, `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`, `loss_tangent`, `dielectric_properties_frequency_hz`

Lengths accept existing unit strings and are normalized to mm. Physical values must be finite and positive. Roughness and loss tangent may also be zero. When `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m` is omitted, consumers may assume 5.8e7 S/m (annealed copper).

Board thickness and copper weight are not duplicated here: `pcb_board.thickness` already holds the board thickness, and each copper layer's `thickness` holds its resolved value.

## Example

Two-layer board, top to bottom, lengths in mm:

```json
{
  "type": "pcb_stackup",
  "pcb_stackup_id": "pcb_stackup_1",
  "pcb_board_id": "pcb_board_1",
  "plated_hole_copper_thickness": 0.02,
  "layers": [
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "top", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    {
      "layer_type": "dielectric",
      "dielectric_type": "core",
      "material_name": "FR-4",
      "thickness": 1.51,
      "relative_permittivity": 4.3,
      "loss_tangent": 0.02,
      "dielectric_properties_frequency_hz": 1000000000
    },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "bottom", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 }
  ]
}
```

## Tests

Each file contains a single test:

- `pcb_stackup_jlc_template`: a JLC04161H-3313 fixture parses through `any_circuit_element`, units normalize to mm, and the JSON round trip is stable.
- `pcb_stackup_optional_material_properties`: optional properties are retained, and zero roughness and zero loss tangent are accepted.
- `pcb_stackup_required_fields`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_layers`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_physical_values`: missing fields, unknown layer types or refs, and zero, negative or non-finite values are rejected.

The README has a new `PcbStackup` section, generated with `bun run generate-docs`. Only the stackup section is committed, without unrelated regeneration drift.

## Validation

`bun test` (475 pass), `tsc --noEmit`, `lint:zod`, `check-snake-case`, `build`, `format`: all pass.

title: Reproduce missing pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad footprints
description: Reproduces a bug where the analyzer fails to determine pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad LED and diode footprints due to small coordinate differences, without changing the analyzers functionality.
body:
## Motivation
Imported two-pad LED and diode footprints can contain tiny coordinate differences between pad centers, even when the pads are intended to form a horizontal or vertical row. analyzePcbPin1Location currently treats these footprints as diagonal and returns null.


Core therefore cannot populate pin1_location, leaving downstream assembly and pick-and-place tools unable to verify or adjust the orientation of polarized components. The analyzer should tolerate small import rounding errors while continuing to reject genuinely diagonal footprints.

This PR only reproduces the issue. It does not change the analyzer.

- Uses the exact imported LED and diode pad geometry.
- Generates SVG snapshots directly from those fixtures and the analyzer's current output.
- Uses `test.failing` to document the expected `topside_left` result without treating the current `null` result as correct.

### LED rectangular pads

![LED pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-led.snap.svg)

### Diode polygon pads

![Diode pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-diode.snap.svg)

- `bun run build`

title: Add polarized option to generic capacitor footprints
description: Adds a polarized option to generic capacitor footprints, allowing for a positive pin marking and specific silkscreen placement without altering existing pad geometry.
body:
Adds `.polarized()` / `_polarized` to generic `cap` footprints. Opting in draws a 0.15 mm silkscreen + beside pin 1, with at least 0.25 mm clearance from copper and body paths. Default/disabled capacitors retain their existing output and pad geometry.

```ts
fp().cap().imperial("0603").polarized().circuitJson()
fp.string("cap0603_polarized").circuitJson()
```

A standalone, smaller alternative to #927: this PR includes only the generic-capacitor flag and its positive-pin-1 marking. It adds no positive/negative pin remapping and changes no radial/electrolytic generators. The cap builder exposes the flag, and the passive definition schema retains it. Contradictory polarized/nonpolarized selections are rejected. Existing origin/rotation and `nosilkscreen` options apply to the new mark.

Validation: **646 tests pass**, production build and changed-file format check pass. New SVG snapshots cover four sizes, opt-in/default/disabled behavior, through-hole holes, transforms, and disabled silkscreen. No new documentation files.

title: Fix nonparallel flex tails in the 3D viewer
description: Fixes rendering issues in the 3D viewer for flex PCB tails with nonparallel bend axes by updating flex-utils and restoring Float32 boundary precision.
body:
Separate encoder and connector tails with nonparallel bend axes fail in the live viewer because it does not supply the board outline needed to resolve independent moving regions. Update bundled flex-utils to 0.0.8 and pass the board-local outline to its existing folding implementation.

Restore Float32 boundary precision when adapting native Three.js meshes so rounded tail edges are classified on the correct moving region instead of remaining flat and forming spikes. This adapter handles Three.js storage precision and mesh transforms; bend-region selection, fold ordering, deformation and CAD transforms remain in flex-utils.

The **Flex PCB → Independent Tails** fixture has a 180° encoder return, a separate 90° connector bend, component markers and stiffeners. Its fractional tail edge reproduces the precision bug. Open [Folded](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--folded) or [Flat](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--flat); right-click **Fold PCBs** to switch states. Regression tests share the fixture and check tail positions, CAD fold/unfold, textures and edge precision.

Apply the repository formatter to the four existing workflow/documentation files reported by CI, including CRLF normalization; workflow behavior is unchanged.

Dependency publication: flex-utils 0.0.8 currently publishes only to GitHub Packages. The public npm registry returns 404, GitHub Packages requires authentication, and jscdn serves tarballs rather than npm registry metadata. Keep the working versioned CDN dependency until flex-utils is published to public npm; replacing it with a bare version now would break clean installs.

Validation: CI passes Format Check, Type Check and Test Node Bundle Load (including the flex regression tests). Repository-wide formatting and the production build also pass locally.

Downloading a hierarchical KiCad project included only the root `.kicad_sch` file. A project with seven child sheets therefore contained just 1 of the 8 required schematic files, leaving the child-sheet references unresolved.

The ZIP includes the root schematic and every child schematic returned by `getOutputFiles()`. The root filename is passed to the converter so child-sheet references and any renamed child files stay consistent.

- Add all converter-generated schematic files directly to the existing ZIP download function.
- Update `@tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import` from `^0.0.15` to `^0.0.20`, which includes the KiCad declarations published after [internal-dynamic-import#42](https://github.com/tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import/pull/42) merged.
- Use `SupportedModuleMap["circuit-json-to-kicad"]` for the loader's KiCad module type.

- Full Bun suite: 417 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed.
- Typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub test, formatting, and typecheck checks passed; Vercel deployment succeeded for `0243fbc`.

description: Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solvestep behavior.

Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solve/step behavior.

**Merge #3155 first.** It contains only the two Bun version upgrades, pinned to 1.4.3. This branch is based on that prerequisite, with separate commits for the runtime implementation and the complex-board parity test.

The new default-effort dataset18 sample01 test covers 115 connections, 279 obstacles, and 205 routed traces. It runs a fresh synchronous solver and a second solver with **four native Bun workers**, with caches disabled. Strict worker mode rejects unavailable registrations/startup failures; 146 dispatched batches prove the test exercises worker execution.

The checks require:
- Byte-identical complete routed SRJ, with no coordinate rounding, ID normalization, sorting, or tolerance.
- Exact high-density routes before downstream phases can hide differences.
- Identical high-density statistics and phase/pipeline logical iteration counts.
- Successful routing, unchanged source input, and a sufficiently complex board.

Both complete outputs have the same SHA-256 hash, printed in the test log. The checked-in snapshot renders both independently produced boards with the standard relaxed-DRC overlay: **UNTHREADED on the left, 4 THREADS on the right**. Both show zero relaxed-DRC errors.

![Dataset18 sample01: UNTHREADED versus 4 THREADS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/7e27c8e680d68feb239ce2b191d1b15d65f2e7df/tests/features/__snapshots__/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.snap.svg)

Run it with:
```sh
bun test tests/features/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.test.ts --timeout 300000
```

A subprocess fixture bypasses the test suite's SVG preload, which replaces global Worker with Node's adapter, so this test exercises Bun's actual native worker pool. The visual snapshot is separate from the exact data comparisons.

Runtime behavior: registered four-node tasks commit in serial node-pop order; budget-crossing tasks replay the exact remaining prefix. Preloaded-copper dependencies remain serial. Bun/Node factories embed generated worker bundles; default/browser imports remain inline and exclude worker payloads. The host owns runtime disposal, and worker errors reject.

Align package.json once from 0.0.56 to the already published 0.0.67 so pver can select 0.0.68; otherwise the existing ten-tag collision limit [stops publishing before PR creation](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/actions/runs/39170393887). Subsequent bumps use the existing bot workflow. No tags are deleted or republished.

Validation: the actual pver 0.0.43 and create-pull-request v5 branch code were exercised against temporary local Git remotes. Detached checkout produces no PR diff; attached main creates a branch containing 0.0.68, with remote main unchanged. No npm package was published during validation. title: Detect transistor LED misalignment
description: Detects misalignment between a transistor and LED in a rail-to-rail indicator branch, ensuring proper alignment for electrical connections.
body:
Q2 and LED4 in the ESP32 GPS tracker's NETLIGHT indicator are separated with perpendicular connected terminals. `TransistorLedAlignmentSolver` emits `TransistorLedNotAligned` when a typed LED and transistor in a rail-to-rail indicator branch cannot read as a straight facing connection.

Stack: #335 (TSX repro) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first. This stack is independent of the fuse/connector stack.

![Tracker indicator before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/28d4e1f4337530a8fd835abc40a9a542e91266a8/tests/cases/__snapshots__/transistor-led-alignment-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The proof comes from [pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker v1.1.0](https://tscircuit.com/pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker?version=1.1.0#schematic). The corrected TSX rotates Q2 and LED4 into a direct vertical branch, aligns R20 with its transistor terminal, and turns/repositions R16 so its supply terminal is above it. Component values, native symbols and all source electrical records are preserved. Tests also verify visible wire continuity. The complete four-part extract reports **zero findings from all analyzers** after correction.

The committed comparison includes all three original findings, with the original and corrected circuits at equal scale, a divider, red markers and diagnostics below. The original repro and a separate complete corrected-network snapshot are retained. This is an extracted network; the full published board has other findings.

The rule requires native `simple_led`, NPN/PNP `simple_transistor`, and a series `simple_resistor` between opposite declared power/ground rails. It uses typed metadata, connectivity and drawn terminal directions; names, labels, hints and pin numbers do not establish roles. It accepts horizontal or vertical straight connections and compact local bends. Separation must exceed the larger of 2 schematic units or twice the LED's largest dimension, with 0.15 units of lateral tolerance for facing pins. Ambiguous/branched connections, feedback, DNP/DNC, conflicting rails, overlapping bodies, separate scopes and incomplete geometry are skipped.

Existing coverage is demonstrated explicitly: fixing only the R20/Q2 alignment and R16 orientation leaves this LED/transistor finding. The low-side-load solver requires a different chip-load/clamp network, and #282's single-pin extension requires already-horizontal facing terminals. [SIM800 Hardware Design v1.09, page 47, Figure 43](https://simcom.ee/documents/SIM800/SIM800_Hardware%20Design_V1.09.pdf#page=47) illustrates a vertical LED/resistor/transistor branch; its resistor is on the other side of the LED, so the proof retains the published board's own connections rather than copying that circuit.

Validation: **273 tests pass**, plus typecheck, build and formatting. Guards cover renamed names/hints/pin numbers, rail flags, branched/feedback connections, missing/duplicate geometry, DNP/DNC, scope, rotation/reflection, compact bends and alignment tolerance. Both corrected SVGs were rendered and visually inspected. Existing unrelated snapshots, dependencies and timeouts are unchanged.

Imports the pcb-spice-pipeline implementation (previously developed in `0hmX/pcb-spice-pipeline`) into the tscircuit org, with its full commit history.

## What it does
Native tscircuit TSX → routed PCB geometry → FastHenry/FasterCap extraction → `@tscircuit/ibis-to-spice` → ngspice → measured waveforms and eye diagrams. Runtime is plain code, no LLM.

- `src/` — geometry extraction, RLGC matrices, SPICE assembly, native IBIS consumption, eye-diagram metrics, CLI (`pcb-spice-pipeline`), `--repeat` determinism check
- `scripts/` — pinned native toolchain setup (`setup-tools.py`), plotting, `prove`/`audit-eye` repeatability proofs, `reproduce.sh`
- `examples/` — straight trace, routed AM3352 JSON, and the real AM3352 DDR TSX eye example
- `tests/` — unit tests plus native/real-board integration tests
- `vendor/` — experimental `@tscircuit/core`/`props` IBIS builds and `ibis-to-spice` tarball
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — Linux CI (not yet exercised; the proof was run on Darwin arm64)

## Usage
```sh
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline --setup
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline index.circuit.tsx
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline --repeat index.circuit.tsx
```
